question: A shopkeeper buys a bag for ₹850 and sells it for ₹1,020. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 850 : 1020 = 85 : 102 = 5 : 6

Profit = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹850

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1020

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 ₹850
 Cost Price

 
 
 ₹1020
 Selling Price

 

 

 
 + ₹170

 Profit = ₹170 → Profit % = 20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = 1020 − 850

⇒ Profit = ₹170

⇒ Profit % = (170 ÷ 850) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (17 ÷ 85) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than Cost Price, Loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Finding SP from Profit %

When Profit % is given, Selling Price = CP × (100 + Profit %) ÷ 100.

Finding CP from Profit %

When Profit % is given, Cost Price = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit %).

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.
